newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end lower; week's first setback.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end lower; week's first setback.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed lower Thursday as investors took profits from the market's sizzling advance and braced for a critical payroll and wage report due Friday.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended 32.51 points lower at 6,976.48 after racing up 265 points since the start of the week. In the broader market, however, advancing issues led declines 1,455 to 1,016 on moderate volume of 459 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The market's performance encouraged analysts, who have watched warily as the broad market failed to follow the lead set by the blue-chip Dow stocks during their furious recovery from a month-long correction.

"The recovery, even in the S&P 500, has really been led by 10 or 15 companies," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "You really want many more stocks participating to have a sustainable advance."
Analysts said the Dow's pause was almost inevitable on the day before the wage and payrolls data, one of the few reports that draw almost universal attention on Wall Street.
A robust report was sufficient to trigger the first sell-off in last summer's correction, and analysts said a surprising number, either way on Friday could easily produce another tempestuous session.
"Could we get another 100-point plus day either way tomorrow? Absolutely," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.

The balance of data this week has been reassuring to investors, showing a strong economy without inflation, the so-called "Goldilocks economy" because its pace is believed to be not too hot and not too cold.
Such an economy is particularly favourable for stocks, which benefit because earnings growth flourishes in a vibrant economy and interest rates can stay low when inflation is subdued.
"It felt like Goldilocks has been resurrected in the last few sessions," Crane said. "But if we get a really strong report tomorrow, she probably fades for a while."
Investors displayed less caution when it came to small-name stocks and technology stocks, two groups whose fortunes rely heavily on prospects for future economic growth.
"Small-cap stocks tend to trade on earnings that are far, far out in the future," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
"I view today as a good sign, because if the market is looking out beyond a year and seeing positive things, that's going to be reflected in small cap prices," she said.

Before Friday's market opens, investors will pore over the contents of the April jobs figures. Many will focus on the report's average hourly earnings component for any sign the economy's robust growth is forcing wages higher.

"For the most part, the inflation watch is focused on the wages," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "The other side of the issue is how do we relate wage increases to productivity growth."
"For now, the market seems comfortable, because we're seeing fast growth but we're not seeing inflation accelerate," he said.

Among individual issues, Aames Financial Corp. tumbled 3-1/8 to 12-1/4 after the mortgage lender warned that a plan to review the pricing of loans made by third party brokers could hurt its future earnings.

Adobe Systems Inc. jumped 2-5/8 to 41-3/4, one day after Standard & Poor's announced Adobe would fill a vacancy in its S&P 500 Index. The index, a benchmark for large cap equities, is used to set investment allocations at many mutual funds.
Hallwood Group Inc. rose 2-5/8 to 27-1/8. The company said it planned to buy back 19.1 percent of its shares for $27.50 per share.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 9.74 points to 1,270.50.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 2.81 points to 798.53. The American Stock Exchange index was up 5.59 to 558.50.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 1.23 to 415.71. The average share was down 13 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,512.405 down 6.881 or 0.09 percent.
